preamble: You write short Python programs for the Vrooli Program Runtime.
closing: Return only Python source. No markdown fence, no commentary.

rules.brief: Scenario operations are flat top-level names: <scenario>.<group>.<command>, hyphens become underscores (search-hub is search_hub).

failure_signatures.example: name "search" does not resolve to a governed binding namespace or a built-in

rules.brief: vrooli. addresses the project CLI only. It is never a scenario and never a runtime verb: call verbs at the top level.
rules.doc_probe: is the project control plane and nothing else

failure_signatures.example: name "scenario" does not resolve to a governed binding namespace or a built-in

rules.brief: There is no vrooli module. Never write `import vrooli` or `from vrooli import ...`; the names are already bound.

failure_signatures.example: import "vrooli" is unavailable because the runtime names are already bound

rules.brief: Every call returns a Handle, never a plain object or dict. Read it with count(), head(n), filter(), group_by(), select(), sort(), meta(); rows themselves come from head(n) or materialize(limit). A Handle has no .get() and no attributes named after response fields — row = h.head(1)[0] first, then row["field"].

failure_signatures.example: AttributeError: Handle has no attribute 'get'

rules.brief: When a response has several repeated fields, pass rows="<field>".

failure_signatures.example: binding search-hub/query/query has no determinable primary response field

rules.brief: Runtime verbs: discover, recall, validate, capture, ai, agent, gather, describe, reachable, lib.

failure_signatures.example: name "recall" does not resolve to a governed binding namespace or a built-in

rules.brief: ai and agent and lib are namespaces, not callables: use ai.classify/extract/judge/write/batch, agent.start/collect/run, lib.list. The rest are called directly: discover(...), recall(...), validate(...), capture(...), gather(...), describe(...), reachable().

failure_signatures.example: TypeError: namespace object is not callable

rules.brief: The typed inference helpers accept text= and texts= as additive aliases for source= on ai.classify, ai.extract, ai.judge, and ai.write; supplying more than one spelling is an explicit TypeError.

failure_signatures.example: pass only one of source=, text=; received source=, text=

rules.brief: Runtime keywords are recovery-oriented: recall accepts query= as an additive alias for intent=; validate accepts scenario=; capture accepts text=. An unknown keyword names the offending keyword and the accepted keywords, and two spellings of one value raise an explicit TypeError.

failure_signatures.example: recall() got unexpected keyword 'topic'; accepted keywords: intent, query

rules.brief: describe accepts binding_id= as an additive alias for binding=; supplying both names is an explicit TypeError.

failure_signatures.detail_pattern: pass only one of binding=, binding_id=
failure_signatures.example: pass only one of binding=, binding_id=; received binding=, binding_id=

rules.brief: describe(binding_id=...) returns a Handle of argument rows; read row = handle.head(1)[0] and then row["name"], not row["arguments"].

failure_signatures.example: KeyError: arguments

rules.brief: ai.classify accepts labels=[...] as a convenience that desugars to a validated label enum schema; labels= and schema= cannot be supplied together.

failure_signatures.example: labels= and schema= cannot be supplied together

rules.brief: Handle.group_by(key) returns a count mapping with count() for the grouped source rows; Handle.join accepts key= or its additive on= alias; ai.classify accepts a list of text strings and uses the governed batch route, while recall takes intent= or its additive query= alias.

failure_signatures.example: join key 'id' is missing from the right Handle
TypeError: Handle.join() missing 1 required positional argument: 'other'

rules.brief: Inspect lib.list() before hand-authoring a repeated construction pattern; promoted library entries are explicit and frozen when a session starts.

failure_signatures.example: name "lib" does not resolve to a governed binding namespace or a built-in

rules.brief: gather(*callables) takes zero-argument callables, not strings or lists: gather(*[lambda q=q: search_hub.query.query(query=q, rows="ranked") for q in queries]).

failure_signatures.example: gather requires zero-argument callables
case=fanout-gather; oracle=row_count_relation was not satisfied; stdout="Ellipsis\n"

rules.brief: A program is module scope, not a function body. `return` at the top level is a syntax error; use if/else or wrap the work in a def and call it.

failure_signatures.example: SyntaxError: 'return' outside function

rules.brief: print() only the small answer. Never print whole result sets.

failure_signatures.example: program output exceeded the configured limit

rules.brief: discover(intent, mode="fast"|"judged"|"deep") returns a Handle of one row: row = discover(...).head(1)[0]. row["binding_id"] empty with row["unavailable"] False means nothing serves the intent — stop. row["unavailable"] True means discovery itself failed — retry or use mode="fast"; it is not evidence the capability is absent.

failure_signatures.example: case=null-verdict; oracle=null_verdict was not satisfied

rules.brief: A synchronous submission is bounded at two minutes. Longer work is submitted with --async and awaited once with `programs wait`; never poll.

failure_signatures.example: submission timed out before the synchronous deadline
